title: Embedding a countable simple extension in an uncountable algebraically closed field
statement: Let $E\subseteq L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension], let $a\in L$, and assume that the underlying set of $E$ is countable (admits an injection into $\mathbf N$). Write $E(a)\subseteq L$ for the intersection of all subfields containing $E$ and $a$. Let $\Omega$ be an uncountable algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], where uncountable means that its underlying set admits no injection into $\mathbf N$, and let $\tau:E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ be a field embedding. Then the underlying set of $E(a)$ is countable, and there is a field embedding $\widetilde\tau:E(a)\hookrightarrow\Omega$ whose restriction to $E$ is $\tau$. No algebraicity or characteristic assumption is made on $L/E$.

proof.text: For $c\in L$ put $S_c=\{P(c)/Q(c):P,Q\in E[T],\ Q(c)\ne0\}$. This is a subfield of $L$: sums and products have denominators $Q(c)V(c)\ne0$, negation negates the numerator, and the inverse of a nonzero $P(c)/Q(c)$ is $Q(c)/P(c)$. It contains $E$ (constant numerators and denominator $1$) and $c$ (numerator $T$). Conversely every subfield containing $E,c$ contains all these quotients. Thus the intersection defining $E(c)$ equals $S_c$. Polynomial evaluation here is the finite sum $P(c)=\sum_i p_ic^i$, with the polynomial operations of [def-weil-polynomial-ring].

proof.text: Fix an injection $E\hookrightarrow\mathbf N$. Finite coefficient lists encode $E[T]$ injectively in $\mathbf N$: encode their entries using this injection and encode a finite list of natural numbers by its length and repeated pairing. Pairs of polynomials are therefore countable. Step 1 presents every element of $E(a)$ by a pair $(P,Q)$ with $Q(a)\ne0$. Assign to each element the least natural-number code of such a pair representing it; different elements have different least codes. This is an injection $E(a)\hookrightarrow\mathbf N$, including when $a\in E$ and when $E$ is finite.

proof.text: First suppose $a$ is algebraic over $E$, meaning that a nonzero polynomial over $E$ vanishes at $a$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]. By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis], $E(a)$ has a finite $E$-basis of size $d$. For any $x\in E(a)$ the $d+1$ vectors $1,x,\ldots,x^d$ are linearly dependent: their $d$ coordinates give a homogeneous system of $d$ linear equations in $d+1$ unknowns, with a nonzero solution by elimination. The resulting relation $\sum_{i=0}^d e_ix^i=0$, with some $e_i\ne0$, proves that $x$ is algebraic over $E$. Thus $E(a)/E$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 09GN, lemma-degree-minimal-polynomial, and Tag 09G1, lemma-field-extension-generated-by-one-element, algebraic case; finite-dimensional dependence argument of lemma-finite-is-algebraic.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] to the algebraic extension $E(a)/E$ from step 3, the given algebraically closed field $\Omega$, and the specified homomorphism $\tau:E\to\Omega$. It supplies a field homomorphism $\widetilde\tau:E(a)\to\Omega$ restricting to $\tau$. It is injective: if $x\ne0$ mapped to $0$, then $1=x x^{-1}$ would map to $0$, contradicting preservation of $1$. Together with step 2 this proves both conclusions in the algebraic case.

source.place: Tag 09GU, lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure; extension of the prescribed base embedding, as stated by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Now suppose no nonzero polynomial in $E[T]$ vanishes at $a$. Regard $\Omega$ as an $E$-extension through $\tau$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-elements-countable], the subset of $\Omega$ consisting of elements algebraic over $E$ for this scalar structure is countable. It is not all of $\Omega$, since otherwise its injection into $\mathbf N$ would contradict the assumed uncountability of $\Omega$. Choose $b$ outside this subset. By [def-weil-algebraic-element], for every nonzero $P\in E[T]$ one has $P^\tau(b)\ne0$, where $P^\tau$ applies $\tau$ coefficientwise. Also $P(a)\ne0$ for every such $P$, by the case assumption.

Steps: (1) E(c) equals the set of rational expressions P(c)/Q(c), elementary, with def-weil-polynomial-ring. (2) Countability by least codes of pairs of coefficient lists, elementary; a code fixes the pair, which fixes the element. (3) The power-basis Mathlib leaf (IntermediateField.adjoin.powerBasis, which needs only algebraicity) gives a finite E-basis; d+1 dependent powers then make E(a)/E algebraic. (4) The IsAlgClosed.lift leaf is applied with the given τ as φ; injectivity via x·x⁻¹=1. (5) Algebraic.countable is applied to Ω viewed as an E-extension through τ; Ω is uncountable, so some b is not algebraic and P^τ(b)≠0 for every nonzero P. (6) The 09G1 rational-function map P(a)/Q(a) ↦ P^τ(b)/Q^τ(b): well defined because PV−RQ vanishes at a and so is 0; it is a ring map, restricts to τ and is injective. The two cases are exhaustive and proof_deps equals the union of all uses. I checked Stacks fields.tex Tag 09G1 (line 357, both kernel cases) and the 09GK counting lemma (line 769). All cited nodes are Mathlib leaves or Mathlib definitions, so no off-unit tool uses arise; nothing cites SGA. The DAG has no duplicate: the nearby nodes on countable-base transcendence cardinality, large algebraically closed extensions and the prime subfield state other facts.
